output.title: Food delivery dispatch
output.description: An invented delivery company, Quayside Eats. Courier pings stream through MQTT and Kafka into a geo index by H3 cell; ready orders are matched to nearby couriers every two seconds, scored by an ETA model, and offered by push. KEDA scales the indexer up to the topic's partitions.

annotations.text: Pings are keyed by H3 cell, so one busy neighbourhood lands on one partition. Partitions cap how many indexers can help.

simulations.title: Friday dinner rush
simulations.description: Orders climb from 30 to 90 a second and couriers report more often. KEDA scales the geo indexer on Kafka lag, and the dispatch matcher hits the maps provider's 50 calls a second: the excess is rejected, so ETAs fall back to the model.

action.text: Two streams meet in dispatch: orders that are ready, and couriers' locations indexed by H3 cell.
The rush starts. Location lag rises and KEDA adds geo indexers, one per partition at most.
Ninety ready orders a second, but the maps API allows 50 calls: the rest are rejected and the matcher uses the model's ETA.
The rush eases. Every ready order got a courier offer.

expectations.label: The maps API rejects calls over its quota

simulations.title: Eight partitions, a stadium's worth of couriers
simulations.description: A stadium lets out and 3,600 pings a second arrive. KEDA wants more geo indexers, but a consumer group can't use more readers than the topic has partitions: eight. Lag grows until the team raises the topic to 24 partitions.

action.text: 3,600 pings a second. Each geo indexer handles about 400.
KEDA scales to eight indexers and stops: the topic has eight partitions, so lag keeps growing.
The team raises the topic to 24 partitions and KEDA's maximum to match. KEDA adds indexers and the lag drains.
